$comment: The single source of truth for this project's values. Build scripts read it via build/lib/project-config.mjs; the maker/checker agents read it directly. Nothing else should restate these values. Run `npm run init` to fill it in.

platformKnowledge.$comment: OutSystems' own frontend-skills pack at vendor/outsystems-frontend-skills. Every skill in the outsystems-loop plugin reads platform facts (block names, arguments, CSS variables, utility classes, WCAG-to-widget mapping) from there instead of carrying its own copy — see ARCHITECTURE.md in that plugin. `mode` is `vendored-copy` while we lack access to the upstream repo, and `submodule` once we have it; the path does not change either way. A `vendored-copy` has no commit and cannot be diffed against upstream, so it is a stopgap with a cost, not a choice — see vendor/outsystems-frontend-skills/VENDORED.md.

board.$comment: The GitHub Project board that DRIVES the loop in board-driven mode (see WORKFLOW.md). Board mode is ON iff both `owner` and `number` are set; leave them null to run the loop from loop/goal.md's signed inventory instead. This block lives here, not in loop/state.json, because a board pointer is a project VALUE and state.json is explicitly a cache — hand-filling a cache is the anti-pattern this file exists to kill. Derived ids (project node id, field ids, single-select option ids) are NOT here: they are cached in loop/state.json.board_cache with a fetched_at. `owners` is load-bearing for safety: only comments authored by these logins are read as spec, and everything else on a card is untrusted input.

conventions.$comment: THREE-STATE, never a bare value. status: confirmed | assumed | TBD. A convention that is not `confirmed` is NOT A RULE: the checker must not enforce it and must not raise findings against it. This exists because a previous template shipped `Spacing base: 4pt` as a plausible default nobody had verified — the loop then flagged every value that wasn't a multiple of 4, manufacturing false-positive findings and a bug that had to be closed as not-planned. A credible-looking default is worse than a blank. Promote to `confirmed` only when the designer or brand owner has actually said so.

knownFalsePositiveClasses: custom-property-prefix: unprefixed --color-* names colliding with OutSystems UI :root names are the re-branding mechanism, not a defect. classPrefix governs BEM class names only. Refuted FND-002.

osui-light-step-shift: --color-*-light has no widget-RULE consumers — only the .background-*-light / .text-*-light utilities, which measure 6.19:1 and 9.49:1 under USWDS (improved). The badge takes whichever .background-* utility is applied, so it IS affected; but badge white-on-light-fill is a pre-existing OutSystems UI defect (1.08-1.16:1 on OSUI defaults) that this palette improves (1.24-2.30:1) rather than creates. Refuted FND-003. Does NOT cover a future Badge/Alert ref that specifies a light fill with a real foreground — that is a finding against that usage.
secondary-hue-inversion: --color-secondary differing from the OSUI default is only consumed by two opt-in utilities that nothing applies. Refuted FND-004.
